records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink (submodule) pointing at commit a5d290951de, which is not a real submodule of this repository and has no .gitmodules entry. Anyone cloning with --recurse-submodules or CI checking out the PR gets a broken/missing submodule checkout; the repo tree is corrupted by an accidental nested-repo artifact.
records.rationale:
The diff adds a new entry `sentry-repo` with mode `160000` (a gitlink/submodule pointer):
```diff
+new file mode 160000
+Subproject commit a5d290951def...
```
but this PR diff does not add or update a `.gitmodules` file to define that submodule’s URL/path. Introducing a gitlink without corresponding `.gitmodules` metadata is a concrete, verifiable change in the tree that can break `--recurse-submodules` checkouts / CI submodule initialization.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only matches the exact string count(), silently skipping aliased forms ("count() as foo"), count(unique(...)), count_if(...), and any derived column a client sends as yAxis. Users querying yAxis=count() as errors (a documented yAxis form with alias) on allowlisted error-upsampled projects receive unweighted counts with no warning, so the upsampled total silently disagrees with the plain count() widget for the same projects — the acceptance criterion 'error counts are upsampled for allowlisted projects' is only met for the single canonical spelling.
records.rationale: In `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`, the transformation is only applied when `column_lower == "count()"` (it lowercases/strips, but does not parse/handle aliases or other count forms). Any yAxis like `"count() as foo"`, `"count_if(...)"`, `"count_unique(...)"`, etc. will fall into the `else` branch and be returned unchanged, so even when `upsampling_enabled` is true in `organization_events_stats.py`, those aggregations will not be upsampled. This is a correctness gap relative to the intent of upsampling counts for allowlisted error queries.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache key is built with Python's built-in hash(tuple(...)), whose value is randomized per process via PYTHONHASHSEED, so the key computed in invalidate_upsampling_cache (and in any other worker process) differs from the key the writer used. Cache invalidation is a cross-process no-op: when an operator removes a project from the allowlist, invalidate_upsampling_cache deletes a key no process ever wrote, and every web worker keeps serving the stale 'eligible' verdict for up to 60 seconds — queries keep summing sample_weight on a project that just left the rollout. It also collapses the cache to per-process entries, defeating the stated performance optimization.
